best_practice_research_context.question: Rust language optimization for release / production
best_practice_research_context.direct_recommendation: Treat Cargo/rustc release-profile, codegen, PGO, and allocator experiments as production release artifact measurements only; all CI/CD/build/test/script lanes remain Buck2, and any selected optimization must be encoded into Buck2 toolchain/target/OCI paths before becoming standard.

official_sources.name: Cargo Book — Profiles
official_sources.establishes: release/custom profile knobs for opt-level, LTO, panic, strip, incremental, and codegen-units; recommends measuring tradeoffs over assuming universal winners

official_sources.name: rustc Book — Codegen Options
official_sources.establishes: rustc -C controls for LTO, opt-level, codegen-units, panic strategy, strip, and related release codegen behavior

official_sources.name: rustc Book — Profile-guided Optimization
official_sources.establishes: PGO is supported by rustc and should be driven from representative profile-generate/profile-use evidence

official_sources.name: std::alloc
official_sources.establishes: Rust has one global allocator per program and #[global_allocator] configures allocator replacement

official_sources.name: Buck2 rust_binary
official_sources.establishes: Buck2 Rust rules expose rustc_flags/linker_flags/env inputs for encoding selected release behavior into Buck2 targets/toolchains

findings: Added a small evaluator/schema/fixtures instead of broad target-discovery machinery.
Target validation intentionally checks Buck2 labels, not Cargo commands.
Trusted controller/dev target inventory is captured before candidate checkout, matching untrusted-input separation expected in merge gates.
Live required context remains a target authority blocker until cloud-ci/oya-ci posts protected status.
BAD fixture models candidate-authored target inventory, empty required targets, malformed target labels, and false green claims.
Evaluator rejects candidate PR bytes as target inventory source.
Root hub and baseline now point to the new schema and fixtures, keeping future agents on a small explicit contract.
Rustfmt, JSON parsing, static fixture assertions, diff hygiene, Buck2 uquery, Buck2 authority scanner, and Buck2 policy target build were run.
Rejected discovering build/test targets from candidate PR bytes because a malicious PR can delete or omit targets and false-green scope.
No secrets or tenant data touched.
Trusted-source separation closes a local candidate-input authority gap.
No performance claim is made; Rust release optimization research remains measurement-only and Buck2-handoff bounded.
Explicit non-claim boundary prevents local fixture greens from being interpreted as live controller readiness.
Evidence records commands and build IDs; PR body will retain blocked local test details.
Supports AC-0.16 automation ratchet through schema/evaluator/fixture mapping.
Supports AC-0.17 by refusing unearned green/ready claims.
